text.en: Believing a 'standard candle' is an object whose apparent brightness (how bright it looks from Earth) is always the same for every such object -- a standard candle's defining property is instead a known, calibrated intrinsic (absolute) luminosity, how bright it actually is; its apparent brightness varies with distance exactly as the inverse-square law predicts, and it is precisely by comparing that known intrinsic luminosity to the observed apparent brightness that the object's distance can be calculated at all.
text.et: Arvamus, et 'standardküünal' on objekt, mille näiv heledus (kui heledana see Maalt paistab) on alati sama iga sellise objekti puhul -- standardküünla defineeriv omadus on selle asemel teadaolev, kalibreeritud sisemine (absoluutne) heledus, kui hele see tegelikult on; selle näiv heledus varieerub kaugusega täpselt nii, nagu pöördruudu seadus ennustab, ning just seda teadaolevat sisemist heledust vaadeldud näiva heledusega võrreldes saab objekti kaugust üldse arvutada.
